verdict.reasoning: Patient reports left arm numbness and tingling for at least 2 weeks: "I've been taking boxing class for a few weeks... it's probably been, I'd say for at least two weeks and it's kind of gotten worse... then the numbing kind of started... I can feel it both in my elbow and then in my arm as well as in my hand" and numbness/tingling in palmar side of 2nd–4th fingers: "it's my second, third and fourth finger... It's the front side."

She describes mild weakness with fine motor tasks and no pain: "I play a little bit of a piano and so I just noticed that it's been kind of harder to get the notes"; doctor: "So you would say there's a mild weakness?" Patient: "Mild, yes... it's not hurting. It's not hurting. It's like numb. I can't feel it."

Patient notes shoulder pain only with movement: "sometimes I will feel it in my shoulder. Like if I try to... move like in boxing and stuff, I will even like maybe feel a little bit of... pain. But I would say if I'm just like resting..."

She reports transient left eye peripheral vision loss for ~20 minutes a few weeks ago: "all of a sudden just couldn't see from... my left eye. Like, I lost some, like a little bit of a field of vision... that just lasted maybe for, I don't know, 20, 20 minutes" and later confirms it happened in the recent past: "a few weeks ago."

She describes a recent viral-like illness about a month ago lasting ~2 weeks: "I also had a really bad cold like a month ago... And then after that, I was sick for probably good, like, two weeks... I think I must have had some kind of like a flu or something."

She reports occasional headaches and attributes them to fatigue: "Sometimes I get headaches, but I think they're just tired headaches... I work too much or... I'll go for a workout and then I'll really just exhaust myself."

She denies neck pain, seizures, and gait problems: Doctor: "Any neck pain at all?" Patient: "No, not. No neck pain." Doctor explains seizures; Patient: "Oh, no, no, no, no. Nothing like that." Doctor: "leg, walking and all this. Normal?" Patient: "Walking is normal. Yeah."
She reports no significant past medical history: "in general, I'm pretty healthy... I don't really have any medical problems."
Occasional ibuprofen use is stated: "I do take ibuprofen just because my, my muscles were sore a little bit... So I've just kind of taken ibuprofen for that."
Vitamin D use is explicitly mentioned: "I just take ibuprofen every once in a while I take vitamin D."
Melatonin use is stated: "vitamin D, I take. And then sometimes I take melatonin to help me sleep."
She is on iron but often forgets to take it (incomplete supplementation): "my GP really wants me to take iron supplements, but... I most of the time I just forget."
Father's hypothyroidism and autoimmune disease: "I know that my dad has. I don't know if it's hypo. I think it's hypothyroidism... he's got some autoimmune stuff going on."
Mother's type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and high cholesterol: "my mom... she's got diabetes, type 2, she's got hypertension, she's got... she's got high cholesterol."
She is physically active and does boxing: "I've started taking this boxing class. I've been taking boxing class for a few weeks" and elsewhere: "I work out a lot."
Smoking status is never mentioned in the transcript; stating she is a non-smoker introduces new information.
Social alcohol use is implied: "I was out, you know, drinking with friends... we kind of went crazy and we were like out partying" in the context of a co-worker’s anniversary celebration.
No vitals or physical examination findings are documented anywhere in the transcript; the encounter is history-based only.

Assessment of progressive left upper limb numbness/tingling/weakness >2 weeks reflects history: "at least two weeks and it's kind of gotten worse" and doctor summarizing "you have definitely having some sort, some form of weakness."

Doctor explicitly incorporates the transient visual loss in assessment: "when you said you can't, your vision went. Peripheral vision was not there for about 20, so. And that with the weakness of the arms, make me think, is there something else going on?"

There is recent viral illness and concern for neurologic symptoms after it, fitting a possible post-infectious picture: she describes a bad cold/flu-like illness, then neurologic symptoms; clinician considers conditions like MS in that context.

Doctor explicitly mentions demyelinating disease (MS) as a differential: "Sometimes, you know, you do get things like ms, multiple sclerosis. So people with multiple sclerosis can have visual problems... and... numbness, tingling."

Urgent neurology referral and likely imaging are stated: "I'm going to do an urgent, very urgent neurology referral... What that might entail is the brain scan and things like that." (MRI is a type of brain scan, so this is a reasonable inference.)

Safety-net advice including weakness progression, visual symptoms, headaches, vomiting, fits, and need for emergency care: "if the weakness progresses to your legs or there's any kind of headaches, vomiting, fits, and your visual symptoms are getting worse and not getting better, then that would be an A" (implying emergency attention).

No immediate pharmacologic therapy; steroids deferred until diagnosis: Patient asks about drugs; Doctor: "No, that's something we can't do. The treatment for it is actually some steroids... But saying that first we need to adopt firm diagnosis."

Doctor educates patient on need for prompt workup: "I think it is quite important that we investigate it a bit more seriously" and "it's good that we know that you've come and spoken to us today and hopefully we'll get things sorted and the ball rolling."
